source_snapshot.procedure: In BMC WebUI Hardware status > Inventory and LEDs, check Chassis information and detail information.
source_snapshot.criteria: Data should be readable and correct.
source_snapshot.deepseek: YES dumps Name and Oem from an assumed FRU_SYS object with insecure curl and calls it SMBus/I2C inventory; no schema proves that claim, no device/address/topology completeness is shown and OEM control members are not bounded.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION correctly requires a vendor-defined SMBus resource/schema and a strict no-probe/no-write boundary, but keeps the finite Project topology and UI/schema mappings as an engineering decision.

old_problem: A populated generic OEM object is not evidence that the WebUI SMBus inventory is complete or correct. SMBus/I2C has no universal device-discovery/identity transaction, active probing can misidentify devices or be interpreted differently by different chips, and raw bus access is outside this WebUI view case. The earlier review found the safety gap but did not parameterize the supported vendor inventory surface.
disposition_reason: Use the actual rendered WebUI as the required evidence plane and, only when documented for this BMC version, a read-only vendor inventory API/DOM as the structured collector. Compare every approved SMBus bus/mux/channel/address/device entry and status to the Project topology without executing raw transfers, address scans, register reads/writes or OEM controls. Missing schema/topology makes execution NOT READY rather than a new decision.
decision_basis: XLSX row 965, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest, historical V3.1 record and adjacent row 966 were directly reviewed; next pending was verified as Functionality row 966 / variant 4e03ed7ba7e596d8.

The Master procedure requires actual WebUI Chassis information/detail and does not authorize `i2cdetect`, `i2cget`, `i2cset`, raw IPMI or an OEM action. Those operations may not be added to make the case executable.

Linux kernel documentation states I2C has no standard way to detect or identify a device at an address and the same transfer may be read by one chip and write by another; blind detection is therefore unsuitable for this production inventory review.

A vendor-documented read-only inventory representation can be normalized into bus, mux/channel, address, type, identity, presence and status, but a generic `Oem` blob or HTTP success alone has no defined coverage.

ED-03, ED-08, ED-11, ED-16, ED-17, ED-19, ED-21 and ED-30 preserve OEM/safety boundaries and visual evidence; ED-33 through ED-38 permit an approved schema/topology package without guessed collectors or coverage substitution.

test_case.test_name: Validate BMC WebUI SMBus inventory against the approved topology without bus probing
test_case.purpose: Verify every Project-required BMC-managed SMBus/I2C device exposed by the approved inventory view is readable, uniquely mapped and correct in the actual WebUI and documented read-only inventory representation, including bus/mux/channel/address, device identity, presence/status and freshness where supported, without issuing any bus transaction or OEM control.
required_package: Immutable SUT/BMC/platform/firmware/WebUI identity and approved definition of the SMBus/I2C inventory scope managed and displayed by BMC
Authoritative topology manifest with logical bus/controller, mux path/channel, 7/10-bit address notation, expected device/type/identity, fitted/absent state and duplicate-address scope
Documented vendor read-only SMBus inventory schema/resource or approved WebUI DOM/table extraction for the exact BMC firmware; a generic Oem object is insufficient
Actual WebUI Hardware status > Inventory and LEDs SMBus table/detail field mapping, pagination/filter/expand behavior and visual capture method
Expected presence/status, unauthorized/unavailable/unsupported/absent and data-freshness semantics plus stable mapping rules when bus numbering is dynamic
Trusted TLS/protected credentials, sensitive topology redaction, evidence storage and explicit denylist of raw bus probes/register operations/OEM actions
test_case.test_command: READ ONLY MANAGEMENT INVENTORY ONLY. Verify immutable target and vendor documentation, then open the actual rendered BMC WebUI Hardware status > Inventory and LEDs SMBus view, expand all required buses/muxes/channels/pages and capture complete table/detail evidence. If and only if the required package names a read-only inventory API or DOM schema for this BMC version, retrieve that exact resource with certificate verification, validate schema/version and ignore all Action/control/write links. Normalize each expected entry into controller/logical bus, durable mux path/channel, address with width/format, device type/name/identity, presence/status and timestamp/freshness; use the approved stable map rather than assuming dynamic Linux bus numbers. Compare completeness and one-to-one uniqueness to the Project topology and reconcile every displayed field with structured evidence. Do not run `i2cdetect`, `i2cget`, `i2cset`, `i2ctransfer`, raw IPMI/OEM commands, sysfs binds/unbinds, register reads/writes, bus recovery, log clearing, reset, reboot or power actions.
test_case.expected_result: Every expected in-scope SMBus device appears exactly once at its approved logical controller/mux/channel/address and exposes the expected identity, fitted/presence state, status and fresh inventory fields in the actual WebUI and documented structured representation. Approved unfitted/unsupported devices use their defined representation; missing, unauthorized, stale and inaccessible remain distinct. No unexpected/duplicate/mis-mapped device or unclassified OEM field exists, and audit evidence proves no bus transaction, probe, control, write, reset or power action occurred.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires the approved vendor schema/UI mapping, complete expansion/pagination, exact topology membership and address-path identity, actual rendered WebUI evidence, correct presence/status/freshness and a no-probe/no-write audit. A generic Name/Oem dump, HTTP success, raw scan or matching device count cannot pass. Missing/extra/duplicate/wrong-path device, unknown schema, ambiguous dynamic bus number, stale/unclassified status or UI/structured/topology mismatch is FAIL. If the vendor inventory schema/UI field map or Project topology is absent, report NOT READY; do not guess an OEM endpoint or probe the bus to force resolution.
safety_gate: Never perform active SMBus/I2C detection or raw transfers. Prohibit i2cdetect/i2cget/i2cset/i2ctransfer, register reads/writes, sysfs bind/unbind, bus recovery and raw IPMI/OEM bus commands.
Use only the documented read-only BMC inventory surface for the exact firmware and ignore/deny every OEM Action, control or write-capable property; a generic `Oem` object is not authorization.
Use certificate-verified protected sessions and do not expose credentials or sensitive bus/address topology in unprotected reports.
Do not equate dynamic Linux adapter numbers with stable Project bus identities; require controller plus mux-path/channel/address mapping.
Retain the actual rendered WebUI table/detail and complete raw documented inventory artifact before normalization/redaction.
Stop on unknown schema, ambiguous address/path, incomplete pagination, write-capable-only surface or freshness uncertainty and do not automatically retry through a raw bus probe.
expected_evidence: Immutable target/BMC/WebUI identity, vendor read-only inventory schema/version and approved complete SMBus topology manifest
Actual rendered WebUI SMBus table/detail visual artifacts with all buses/mux paths/channels/pages expanded
Complete raw documented inventory/DOM/API artifacts with timestamps, certificate result, schema validation and protected hashes
Normalized per-device matrix of stable controller/mux path/channel/address, type/identity, presence/status/freshness and Project expectation
Explicit accounting of fitted, unfitted, unsupported, inaccessible, missing and unexpected entries plus UI/structured parity
Preserved audit/log evidence and no-probe/no-transfer/no-control/no-write/no-reset/no-power proof with engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: No bus or system mutation is intended. On unknown schema, incomplete inventory, ambiguous address/path, stale status or mismatch, stop and preserve/redact evidence and obtain the approved vendor schema/topology. Do not fall back to an address scan, register access, OEM control, bus recovery, log clear, reset, reboot, power-cycle or automatic retry.

source_conflict.reason: The Master clearly asks for SMBus information readability/correctness in WebUI. DeepSeek's unsupported generic-OEM interpretation is incomplete guidance, not a source contradiction.

blocked.reason: A safe WebUI/vendor-inventory comparison is technically defined without raw probing. Schema, topology and field mappings are finite Project prerequisites.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: BMC-managed SMBus scope; authoritative bus/mux/channel/address/device topology; documented read-only vendor schema or UI DOM/table map; presence/status/freshness rules; trust/redaction and OEM-control denylist.
pending.execution_status: NOT STARTED; READ-ONLY BMC SMBUS INVENTORY REVIEW ONLY; NO API, WEBUI, BUS PROBE, REGISTER, OEM CONTROL OR DUT ACTION EXECUTED

external_authorities.title: Linux kernel: Implementing I2C device drivers
external_authorities.application: Explains that I2C has no standard device presence/identity detection and a transfer may be interpreted differently by different chips, supporting the strict no-probe boundary.

external_authorities.title: Linux kernel: I2C userspace interface
external_authorities.application: Documents dynamically assigned adapter numbers and that userspace device access performs real I2C/SMBus transactions; those interfaces are deliberately excluded.

external_authorities.title: DMTF Redfish Resource and Schema Guide 2025.3
external_authorities.application: Provides standard resource discovery/schema context; no standard Redfish SMBus-inventory resource is presumed, so vendor schema approval is required.

project_authority: The vendor/Project package defines the safe read-only BMC inventory surface and stable SMBus topology. Its absence prevents execution/PASS but must not be bypassed by guessing OEM data or probing the physical bus.
